visualReview.notes: Inspected the octagonal log bastions, projecting gun floors, shingle roofs, cedar stockade, two gates, bell tower and principal courtyard buildings. The southwest street view shows the timber tower and stockade silhouette observed in the original watercolor, historic engraving and period photograph.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the dated placement from all approaches and from above, the two bastions and wall connections, the bell tower and Fort Street gate, the raised whitewashed buildings and the north warehouses. The historic viewer capture exercised model unloading.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 25 medium-fi renders across daylight and late light, views at different distances, four authored levels, two bastions and detail views. The wall, court, gates and towers remain in every level. Street and closeup retain individual timber detail.

geographicReview.notes: Fawcett and the commemorative alignment place the east gate near Government and Fort, and the northwest wall along the historical line by Bastion Square. Used the original 512 m terrain and inspected the unmasked field independently. Modern-grade records constrain the site slope. Historic footing heights, yard grades and the west extent are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Fort Victoria as it stood in September 1860, with the two log bastions, cedar palisade, Fort Street gates, bell tower, and researched exterior courtyard buildings and paths.
fidelityReview.notes: The dated Crease watercolor and period publication establish the southwestern tower. Five period views in Fawcett’s book provide the northeastern bastion, cedar stockade, whitewashed hipped warehouses and houses, east gate and open timber bell tower. Reconstructed dimensions and the locations of individual court buildings are approximate.

imageryReview.notes: Verified the exact local Qualla watercolor against Commons originals, the artist and archive identification, and the matching published 1862 engraving. Independently verified and inspected five images bound to the original 1912 Toronto book and its public-domain catalog record.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: September 1860 dated exterior of the Fort Victoria stockade, the northeast and southwest bastions, both gates, bell tower and principal courtyard structures.

limitations: Historical exterior of Fort Victoria as it stood in September 1860, before the removal of the northeast bastion and adjoining stockade in December. Building footprints, gate positions within their street alignments, exact gun-floor dimensions, and the disposition of minor structures are estimated from documented historic orientation, period views and the original building descriptions.

Original source terrain is preserved. The fort’s yard, footings and original shoreline relationship are approximate because the height field represents present-day Victoria. The model covers the enclosure and its principal courtyard buildings. External harbor facilities and modern city development are outside the model.

No source image is embedded. Researched exteriors include the buildings, part of the fort road, two gates, two octagonal bastions, bell tower and cedar stockade. Interiors and archaeological foundations are outside the modeled scope.
